Build container images FROM an official NGC base and run docker build with --pull so the base layer is fresh.
Validate collective bandwidth after every driver change with a two-node run before trusting any benchmark number.
Before buying an EC2 capacity block, confirm the instance type and interconnect requirement of the workload.
kubectl apply on a GPU node pool must be followed by a fresh-pod check before any latency baseline.
Pin the network installer version in the image build and re-check upstream before each release.
Register a PreToolUse hook with an explicit timeout and make it always exit 0, so a slow or broken hook never blocks the tool call.
pkill -f matches your own shell's command line too; resolve the PID first and kill by PID, in a separate step from the relaunch.
A loose grep over tool output matches your own command line; anchor the pattern or filter with a bracketed first letter.
After pushing, verify the commit's author login on the remote; a noreply address silently changes the attribution.
Never rebase a shared branch in place; rebase onto a fresh topic branch and force-with-lease only your own branch.
Scripts that delete must guard every variable a path is built from, or an empty variable turns the target into the filesystem root.
A nested .git directory inside the working tree is staged as an embedded repository by a blanket add; remove it or make it a submodule first.
Parse only the porcelain form of git status in scripts; the human form changes between versions.
Tag every container image with the git commit it was built from, never only latest.
Tag every container image with the build date, never only latest (superseded wording).
Pin docker base images to a digest in every build file (dormant twin).
